A critical-path gap runs from the critical producer's body-done stamp to the consumer's deps-ready stamp.
The trace stamps three times per task: taken (`etx/codegen/kernel.py:264`), deps ready (`kernel.py:314`,
immediately after the phase-1 barrier at `kernel.py:313`), body done (`kernel.py:333`, after the per-wave
store drain at `kernel.py:324-326` and the barrier at `kernel.py:332`). The producer's **arrive is emitted

26.claim:
- **Flag poll**: thread 0 of wave 0 loops on the event word with an agent-scope atomic load, `s_sleep(8)`
  backoff, abort check every 256 polls (`etx/runtime/include/etx/primitives.h:19-25`;
  `etx/machine/arch/gfx942.yaml:38,45,92`), emitted per grid at `kernel.py:290-292` from
  `_wait_code` (`kernel.py:77-94`).
- **Acquire**: on poll success, an L1/L2 invalidate (`kernel.py:301-307`; `buffer_inv sc1`,

partitions (event counts [4]); router -> topk needs all 256 router rows before any selection (counts [256]);
topk -> moe_up is already the XCD-local replica at the 1.08 us floor. The cross-XCD premium over 1.00
(medians 1.40-1.96) is consistent with the second fabric hop of the flush, but the split between that hop,
the poll granularity and the touch barrier is **[U]** — the trace cannot separate them (section 5).

97.claim:
1. **The chain pays the boundary count, not an above-floor price.** Every free-consumer edge measures
   1.08-1.20 us same-XCD and 1.40-1.96 cross-XCD (section 2), against the measured 1.00 us/edge floor
   (`docs/BUDGET-2026-10-01.md:161`) and fabric one-ways of 642/742 ns (`gfx942.yaml:69-70`). Nine
   boundaries per layer times 48 layers at that floor is most of the 871.0 us no matter what protocol moves
   the bits. Fewer boundaries means fusing bodies, and fusion deletes only the flag round trip: the drain
   and the publication survive inside the fused body for every non-owner consumer
   (`docs/PLAN-300TOKS-2026-10-11.md:66-68`).
2. **The busy half is work conservation under full-barrier events.** Consumer grids are as wide as producer
   grids, every consumer gates the next phase (event counts [256], [24]), and only 6-14 of 38 workers per
   XCD are free at a boundary (section 3, (ii)). Some consumer on the path must start behind a producer on
   the same worker; 13 of 48 critical moe_up -> moe_down consumers sit on the critical producer's own
   worker (`account.txt:62`). The one measured attempt to move the fetch earlier cost +0.095 ms
   (`docs/BUDGET-2026-10-01.md:257`).
3. **The escapes are redesigns, not protocol changes.** Narrowing a consumer grid to the idle pool
   lengthens its bodies proportionally (fewer workers stream the same bytes per phase). Fusing the wide
   pairs moves the wait mid-body: the MoE fold is an XCD-local all-to-all of 24 producers (event E_8,
   counts [24]), so a fused moe_up+moe_down task still polls the same flag between its halves.
97.note: Reviewed attributed fact/identifier and its stated conditions; assertions recheck the literal support. Derived values use the displayed arithmetic; associated citations can jointly supply inputs.

119.claim:
Three facts explain the per-XCD shape:
1. **prep, attn and reduce run only on XCD 0-3.** Their grids have 4, 20 and 4 tasks (`results_vlbest2_2026-10-10/b_all/plan.json`, `types` and `descs`) [M]. Tasks 0-127 have the rows and are on XCD 0-3. Tasks 128-255 are on XCD 4-7 and have no row. Their bodies take 0.28 us, against 5.20 us on XCD 0-3 (median over all layers) [M]. The router finish skew between XCDs is about 6 us in every layer (`docs/xcd-timeline-2026-10-11/report.txt:459,468,477`).
3. **The streaming phases use 24 or 32 of the 38 workers of each XCD.** qkv, o_proj, router and moe_down have 256 tasks, moe_up has 192 (`docs/xcd-timeline-2026-10-11/latency.txt:5-13`). No worker gets two tasks of one grid in the whole step [M].

149.claim:
**Upper bounds for the remaining cache levers [E].**
1. **KV in the Infinity Cache.** The attention bytes at 4.3 TB/s take 24.1 us on the critical path (`account.txt:48`). At the Infinity Cache rate of 11.9 TB/s (`docs/SURVEY-2026-09-29.md:17`) they take `24.1 x 4.3 / 11.9 = 8.7 us`. The largest saving is `24.1 - 8.7 = 15.4 us`, 0.35% of the span. The streaming benchmark shows a smaller effect at 104 MB: 3.43 TB/s cold, 3.66 warm and 3.74 from the Infinity Cache (`results_2026-09-27/vlnext/overlap.log:6`). attn is latency-bound: its phase reaches 7.8% of the bandwidth (`bandwidth.txt:9`) **[17.1% of its own 3.67-XCD ceiling, section 8.1; the latency-bound conclusion is unchanged]**.
2. **The latency phases' loads.** Their activation loads are coherent, so they go past the XCD's L2 by design (`etx/codegen/kernel.py:296-299`). Cross-XCD data must take that path, so a higher L2 hit rate cannot shorten these hops. The round trip under load is 0.69 to 0.73 us at every level, L2, MALL or HBM (`docs/MODEL-vllm-kernels.md:321`). Queueing sets it, not the cache level.
3. **Cacheable weights.** fleet made the router and kv_b weights cacheable on the same GPU. The result was 18% slower, because the working set passed the 4 MB per-XCD L2 cliff (`~/code/fleet-mi300x/docs/STATUS.md:81,233`). fleet's idle-worker prefetch into the Infinity Cache gave no gain (`STATUS.md:72`).

172.claim:
1. **Intra-body stamps.** The bytes and machinery split of every body is an estimate (section 2.1). An optional second trace level could stamp, in the DSL tiles, the first weight load issued, the last weight load returned and the start of the store drain. The imported attention and reduce bodies cannot carry stamps without a change to the imported code [U].
2. **An arrive stamp.** The arrive after `tr[2]` is not stamped (`etx/codegen/kernel.py:333-335`). It is inside the 233.8 us of late edges and inside every gap. One more int64 per trace row would measure it. The row is now 9 int64 (`etx/tools/timeline.py:71-78`, 72 B per task).
3. **A poll-success stamp in phase 1.** It would split each gap into visibility and the rest: touch, acquire, context setup and the barrier. It would show whether the touch is exposed in the busy-consumer edges. A cheaper first test exists: an A/B of the `-DETX_NO_TOUCH` build (`etx/codegen/kernel.py:287`). `docs/OPTIMISATIONS.md:27` says the touch was never isolated after `ETX_VL_COH`.
4. **Per-phase counters.** rocprofv3 reports one value per dispatch, and one dispatch is a whole step. No tool gives L2 hits per phase. rocprofv3 thread trace could time each wave's instructions. Its support on this VF is [U].
5. **An Infinity Cache counter.** None of the data sets has one. Section 3 step 1 checks whether the VF exposes one.
6. **Fixed in this report:** `etx.tools.timeline` grouped the low-bandwidth time by phase kind with a regex that kept the `_x` suffix of replicated grids. Each `topk_N_x` was a separate kind, so topk dropped out of the list. topk is in fact the largest low-bandwidth kind at 401.5 us. The fix is at `etx/tools/timeline.py:296`. The same suffix also gave each topk layer its own colour in the HTML page (`timeline.py:497-499`). A test covers the grouping (`tests/test_timeline.py`).
7. **Session fetch.** `tools/session.sh:89` excludes `b_*/`, so a fetched session has no `plan.json` and no `vl_plan.txt`. This report had to borrow the plan of another session and check it row by row. A copy of both files to the session root, as `qwen300.py` already does for `compile.log`, `hipcc.log` and `compiler_version.txt`, would remove that step.
8. **Trace every timed build.** The anchor session timed a build that it never traced. A session that traces the build it times removes the build caveat of section 0. qwen300 does this (section 6).

184.claim: The per-phase bandwidth shares above divide each phase's achieved GB/s by the whole device's 4.3 TB/s. 199.claim: **L2 (4 MB per XCD, private).** A prefetch lands in the L2 of the XCD that issues it, so an L2 window only works when prefetcher and consumer are the same XCD. What fits per XCD: qkv, o_proj, moe_down and everything smaller; moe_up (6.29 MB) and a whole layer (14.5 MB) do not. Fleet hit this cliff on the same GPU: making 113 MB of weights cacheable pushed the working set past the 4 MB per-XCD L2 and ran 18% slower (fleet `docs/STATUS.md:81,233`).

200.claim: **The window is one layer, and what governs it is the 256 MB MALL minus the 104 MB resident KV cache.** In L2 the window is at most one moe_down-sized phase per XCD, governed by the 4 MB cliff. One phase-specific limit governs separately: moe_up's *selected* weights are 50.33 MB, but which experts are selected is only known when topk finishes, 1.08 us (median) before moe_up starts (`account.txt:72`). Prefetching all 128 experts instead of the 8 selected is `50.33 x 128 / 8 = 805.3 MB` per layer [E] (`examples/llm/configs/qwen3-30b-a3b.json:1`: 128 experts, 8 per token), 5.3 times the MALL headroom. moe_up is therefore not prefetchable in practice; its window collapses to the 1.08 us topk-to-moe_up gap.

208.claim: **The eviction risk, stated plainly:** if a prefetched line is evicted before the consumer reads it, the line is read from DRAM twice — once by the prefetcher, once by the consumer — and the step is slower, not faster, by the prefetch's own traffic. The experiment detects this two ways: (a) `rocprofv3`'s `TCC_EA0_RDREQ_DRAM_sum` per dispatch, compared against the control arm; the baseline is 48.9-50.9 M requests at 119.5 B per request, one fetch per weight byte (`results_2026-10-01/round15/cache.txt:3-5`, `ntc.txt:1-3`, `results_2026-10-01/round15/FINDING.md:55-56`) [M], so any excess over the known 6.19 GB is re-reads; (b) the pass-C rate in the survival arm of the microbenchmark (section 5), which falls back to the cold rate if the window was evicted.

211.claim: **Compute: no pair of phases is independent.** The decoder layer is a serial chain, qkv -> prep -> attn -> reduce -> o_proj -> router -> topk -> moe_up -> moe_down -> next layer's qkv (the layer order of `account.txt:82-143`), and every consecutive pair carries a measured dependency edge in the trace (`account.txt:62-79`). The brief's example needs a correction here: layer N's `attn` and `reduce` are indeed dependent, but layer N's `moe_down` and layer N+1's `qkv` are **not** independent either — the trace measures 47 such edges and 190.2 us of gaps on them (`account.txt:63,65`) [M], because qkv_{N+1} reads the residual stream that moe_down_N produces (the input/residual norm is folded into qkv). What is independent of everything is the **weight stream**: weights are constants, so any phase's weights can be loaded during any earlier phase, subject to capacity (section 1) and to the addresses being known (moe_up/moe_down only after topk).

220.claim: Why the realised value will be lower than even 63 us: (a) the +9% was measured with no co-running consumer stream; during P2/P3 the prefetch competes with the running phase for the same HBM, and the measured price of filling idle bandwidth next to a latency chain is a doubling of its round trip, 1.52 -> 3.08 us (`overlap.log:15-16`, split placement, background 4.31 TB/s) — the latency phases carry 396.4 us of exposed hops [E], so even a 10% slowdown there (~40 us) eats most of the central estimate; (b) the MALL window sits at 86% occupancy with the KV cache, so some eviction is likely and every evicted line is read twice (section 2); (c) if NT consumer loads cannot hit the prefetched lines [U], the consumers must go cacheable, risking the fleet 18% L2-cliff loss; (d) fleet already measured this mechanism's two direct ancestors on the same GPU: idle-worker prefetch into the Infinity Cache gave no gain, and prefetch across the event wait was 4% slower (fleet `docs/STATUS.md:72,30`).

224.claim:
1. **The idle is a symptom, not a resource.** A worker idles because its next task's inputs do not exist yet. Section 3 shows there is no independent compute to give it: every consecutive phase pair is dependency-linked in the trace, including the pair the brief calls independent (moe_down_N -> qkv_{N+1}, 47 measured edges, `account.txt:63,65`). The only thing that can move into the idle time is weight traffic, and weight traffic's value is bounded by the cache-rate delta, measured at +9% at layer size and negative at window size (`overlap.log:3-8`).
2. **Filling the idle ports has a measured price on the work that matters.** The fold benchmark on this GPU: the latency chain's round trip went 1.52 -> 3.08 us when a background stream filled the idle bandwidth (`overlap.log:15-16`). The latency phases carry 396.4 us of exposed hops [E]; a slowdown there is paid on the critical path, while the prefetch benefit is bounded at 63-121 us [E]. The mechanism can be net negative even when it works.
3. **It has been tried, twice, on this GPU.** Fleet's idle-worker prefetch of routing-independent weights into the Infinity Cache: no gain, 4.84 vs 4.80 ms, with the reason recorded — the per-CU streaming rate (~30 GB/s) caps what idle workers can pull, and the phases that would benefit are latency-bound, not byte-bound (fleet `docs/STATUS.md:72`). Cross-task prefetch across the event wait: 4% slower (fleet `docs/STATUS.md:30`). And ETX's own touch hook is already the within-phase version of this mechanism — waves 1-15 pull the task's first weights into L2 during the dependency wait (`etx/codegen/kernel.py:283-290`) — and its value after `ETX_VL_COH` was never isolated (`docs/OPTIMISATIONS.md:27`).
4. **Caching cannot shorten the latency that dominates.** The loaded round trip is level-independent (`docs/MODEL-vllm-kernels.md:321`), so residency touches only bandwidth exposure, which section 4 bounds at 2.7% of the span in the most favourable case.

232.claim: The evidence that settles it, in order: the existing `-DETX_NO_TOUCH` A/B (a 20-second existing-switch probe that prices the mechanism's already-shipped within-phase form, `docs/OPTIMISATIONS.md:27`); phase 1's S1/S2 (does a prefetched window survive the step's own NT traffic at all) and S3/S4/I1 (is there a benefit, and what does it cost the latency chain); then phase 2's KEEP vote. If S1 or S2 fails, the idle time is provably not usable by this mechanism at this model shape, and the counter-argument holds. If phase 1 passes and phase 2 still misses KEEP, the idle time is usable in principle but worth less than 0.030 ms — and the 300 tok/s question must be answered elsewhere.

416.claim:
**6. Prefetch and XCD switching cannot close the gap.**
VERDICT 6 WEAK
Decided by: `results_2026-09-27/vlnext/overlap.log:11-16`.
Evidence: three of the four supporting reasons are misread, and the bound's arithmetic overstates it:
- **The doubling.** 1.52 -> 3.08 us is at a 4.31 TB/s background (:15-16). At the 0.67-1.71 TB/s the prefetches would add, the same bench gives 3.24 -> 3.32-3.36 us, +2.5-3.7% (:11-13).
- **Level-independent latency.** The cited figure is loaded, with 303 CUs streaming (MODEL:321). The latency phases run lightly loaded, where an idle round trip costs 0.143/0.261/0.412 us from L2/MALL/HBM (`docs/MODEL-vllm-kernels.md:320`).
- **86%.** That is the MALL occupancy *with* a prefetched layer added (PF:32). The KV cache alone fills `103.7/256 = 40.5%` [E].
- **The bound's arithmetic.** `702.3 x 0.172` treats a rate gain as a time saving. The time saving is `1 - 3.61/4.23 = 14.7%`, so the upper end is **102.9 us**; the central value is `1 - 3.43/3.74 = 8.3%`, **58.2 us** [E].
416.note: Reviewed attributed fact/identifier and its stated conditions; assertions recheck literal support. Derived values use displayed arithmetic; associated citations can jointly supply inputs.

461.claim: Within claim 9's own arithmetic, no single figure can flip the verdict. One pool would have to grow by `0.847 - 0.254 = 0.593 ms`. The nearest candidate, the prefetch bound, would have to reach `0.847 - 0.110 - 0.023 = 0.714 ms`. That is 6.9 times its corrected 102.9 us upper end (5.9 times the stated 120.8), and more than the entire 702.3 us of byte time in qkv, o_proj and moe_down [E]. The 0.847 ms need cannot be wrong by that much: the on-arm rounds span 0.011 ms (`R/job2_run4.log:144`).

462.claim: The figure that actually decides reachability is the **attention+reduce ceiling, 0.236 ms** [E] (`RB:7-8`), resting on the round11 attn/reduce floors of 2.92/2.81 us (`docs/FLOORS-2026-10-08.md:241-242`). If the attainable correct attention+reduce cut is below **0.142 ms** (2.96 us/layer, or 28% of their 10.645 us/layer critical bodies, `RB:7-8`) [E], 300 tok/s is out of reach even with every other row at its ceiling. The figure would have to be overstated by `0.236 - 0.142 = 0.094 ms` (40%) to flip the paper envelope from "reachable" to "not". The floors omit LDS and MFMA work (PLAN:23), so an overstatement of that size is plausible, not exotic.
